description: Mining in Society explores where the materials in everyday life come from: minerals and their uses, mines in your region, mine hazards and safety gear, abandoned mines, reclamation and sustainability, future mining and recycling, and careers.

safety.note: Never enter an abandoned mine or quarry — stay out and stay alive.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. The 2026 update turned requirement 8 into a choice of career options. A forum report said requirement 5 should read as a choice of one option; check the current wording.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Minerals and their uses
requirements.summary: Identifying minerals and products that use them, and mining’s role in food production.

requirements.title: Mapping mines
requirements.summary: Marking mining operations in your state or region and what each produces.

requirements.title: Mine hazards
requirements.summary: Hazards of mining and the protective equipment miners use.

requirements.title: Abandoned mines
requirements.summary: The dangers of abandoned mines and quarries.

requirements.title: A mine experience
requirements.summary: One option, such as a virtual tour, museum exhibit, active mine visit or local mine history.

requirements.title: Sustainability
requirements.summary: Environmental controls and reclamation at modern mines.

requirements.title: Mining’s future
requirements.summary: Ocean and space mining, recycling metals and minerals, and commodity prices.

requirements.title: Careers
requirements.summary: One option exploring mining careers, such as interviewing a mining worker.
